start_here: Say to your AI: "Check my computer at 203.0.113.20 from inside: how full are its disks, and does its engine still hold me?" It runs tool:check-a-computer-from-inside with that computer's row and tells you each disk past 85% or 92%, and each engine that lost its person (holding them again first).
no_lists_because: It keeps nothing: it reads one computer and answers what it read and its findings. The workflow that runs it every fifteen minutes keeps the readings and tells the findings.
instructions: 1. Read the computer's row from wherever you keep it: its name, address, runs and SSH host key.

2. Call tools:run with tool tool:check-a-computer-from-inside and input {name, address, runs, host_key}. The administrator key is the held value server-administration-ssh-key; it reaches only the hosts its vault entry names.

3. Read findings: disk-filling (warn) and disk-nearly-full (alert), engine-held-no-person (warn when it was held again and holds them now, alert when not), engine-not-answering and unreachable (alert), due-time-wakes-without-a-teller (alert: an engine has switched-on due-time wakes but no switched-on tool:notice-when-something-shows-up wake named keep-noticing or keep-noticing/<name>, so nothing tells them when due) and wake-book-not-read (warn: the engine's wakes could not be read).

4. To see a finding without making it, give pretend: {disks: {"/": 93}}, {engines: {"<unit>": 0}} or {wake_books: {"<unit>": [wake, ...]}} or {unreachable: true}; a pretended engine is never asked to hold anyone.
5. To check every computer every fifteen minutes and tell each finding, run workflow:check-every-computer-from-inside.
